<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Step S1 of #62243: move the Mooncake P2P connector metadata and wire structs into `mooncake/metadata.py` and `mooncake/protocol.py`. Definition-site move, no behavior change.

## Claims

- Definition-site move: `ReqId`, `TransferId`, `PullReqMeta`, `SendBlockMeta`, `MooncakeConnectorMetadata` move to `mooncake/metadata.py`; `MooncakeXferMetadata`, `MooncakeXferResponseStatus`, `MooncakeXferResponse` move to `mooncake/protocol.py`.
- Wire formats unchanged: every msgspec field order, default, `omit_defaults`, and status-code value (`FINISH=0`, `CONTINUE=1`, `ERROR=2`, `LAYOUT_MISS=3`) is byte-identical to `main`.
- Behavior unchanged: no logic edits; `mooncake_connector.py` still re-exports every moved name, so existing `from ...mooncake_connector import MooncakeXferMetadata` imports keep working.
- One rename inside the moved code: `MooncakeConnectorMetadata.reqs_not_processed` becomes `transfers_not_processed`, with the scheduler field it is assigned from.

## Validation

Tests (before = `main` at `da9134bc8`, after = this branch, same command, macOS, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`):

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=<worktree>:<vllm>/scratch \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -q
```

- Before: `413 passed` in 92.44s (and `413 passed` in 93.68s on a second run of the same tree).
- After: `413 passed` in 91.40s.

`-p no_mps_cleanup_plugin` is only a local workaround for a macOS-only teardown segfault in `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()`; it is applied to both runs and touches no repository file.

Lint and types:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/metadata.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/protocol.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
```

All hooks pass: `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos`, `mypy` (oldest supported Python), `check-spdx-header`, `check-forbidden-imports`, `check-root-lazy-imports`, `check-test-tethering`, plus the remaining hooks that apply to Python files.

Name-level checks:

- Moved code is byte-identical to `main`: the `metadata.py` body matches `mooncake_connector.py` lines 99-100 and 658-714 of `main` exactly, and the `protocol.py` body matches lines 608-657 exactly (`diff` of the extracted regions is empty).
- Public namespace of `mooncake_connector` is unchanged apart from `IntEnum`, which was an incidental re-export of `from enum import IntEnum` and is now unused there (ruff flagged it). Every name the module defined before is still importable from it:

```bash
python -c "from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake.mooncake_connector import MooncakeXferMetadata, PullReqMeta, SendBlockMeta, MooncakeConnectorMetadata, MooncakeXferResponse; print('ok')"
```

## Details

Names moved, and their new homes:

| Definition | New module |
| --- | --- |
| `ReqId`, `TransferId` | `mooncake/metadata.py` |
| `PullReqMeta`, `SendBlockMeta` | `mooncake/metadata.py` |
| `MooncakeConnectorMetadata` | `mooncake/metadata.py` |
| `MooncakeXferMetadata`, `MooncakeXferResponseStatus`, `MooncakeXferResponse` | `mooncake/protocol.py` |

Dependency direction is one-way and acyclic: `protocol.py` imports `ReqId`/`TransferId` from `metadata.py`; `metadata.py` imports `KVConnectorMetadata` from `..base` and `EngineId` from `kv_connector/utils.py`, and does not import `protocol.py`. `mooncake_connector.py` imports both and keeps them in its namespace, so tests and any external imports of those names are unaffected.

The rename: `MooncakeConnectorMetadata.reqs_not_processed` holds `set[TransferId]`, not request ids, while the identically named field in `nixl/metadata.py` does hold `set[ReqId]`. Since the definition moves here, it is renamed to `transfers_not_processed` together with the scheduler field assigned into it (`_transfers_not_processed`). Seven lines in the package and one attribute name in an existing assertion in `test_mooncake_connector.py`; no assertion semantics change, no wire impact.

Names inside the moved code that were left alone, and why:

- msgspec field names in `protocol.py` are wire keys; renaming any of them changes the encoded format.
- `reqs_to_recv` / `reqs_to_send` / `need_send` / `sent` / `sending` / `PullReqMeta` / `SendBlockMeta` / `d_req_id` / `p_req_id` keep their names: `reqs_to_recv` and `reqs_to_send` are shared with `nixl/metadata.py`, and #61974 constructs `SendBlockMeta(p_req_id=...)` and inserts `aborted` next to `sending`, so renaming those here would only move conflict into that PR.
- The `mooncake_` prefix in `mooncake_connector.py` / `mooncake_utils.py` and the `MooncakeXfer*` class names belong to the later steps: #62243 keeps `mooncake_connector.py` as the compatibility shim until `connector.py` exists in S5.

Out of scope, deliberately: the worker split, scheduler split, bootstrap helpers, region planning, facades, and a new `connector.py` (steps S2-S5 of #62243). The two wire protocols are not unified here.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- No other open PR moves these definitions; no open PR references #62243 in its body.
- #57309 touches the same file only to swap the spec-classification helpers to framework spec kinds; it moves no metadata or wire struct, and none of its hunks overlap the renamed lines.
- #61974 adds `mooncake_pull_connector.py` and a `compat.py`; its compatibility hash stays where that PR puts it, and is not absorbed here.

+
+ReqId = str  # Internal scheduler request ID
+TransferId = str  # KV transfer coordination ID (shared by P/D)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PullReqMeta:
+    d_req_id: ReqId
+    transfer_id: TransferId
+    local_block_ids: list[list[int]]
+    remote_engine_id: EngineId
+    remote_bootstrap_addr: str
+    # Set expire time to avoid infinitely sending requests.
+    expire_time: float = float("inf")
+    # Designed for one D pairing to multiple P
+    pull_tasks_count: int = 0
+    # Set once any worker reports a failure, so a success from another worker
+    # for the same request is not counted afterwards.
+    failed: bool = False
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SendBlockMeta:
+    p_req_id: ReqId
+    transfer_id: TransferId
+    local_block_ids: list[list[int]]
+    ready: asyncio.Event
+    expire_time: float = float("inf")
+    need_send: int = 0
+    sent: int = 0
+    sending: int = 0
+
+
+class MooncakeConnectorMetadata(KVConnectorMetadata):
+    def __init__(self):
+        # Use (engine_id, dp_rank) to group reqs with same dp.
+        # See comments in MooncakeBootstrapServer.
+        self.reqs_to_recv: dict[EngineId, dict[ReqId, PullReqMeta]] = defaultdict(dict)
+        self.reqs_to_send: dict[ReqId, tuple[TransferId, list[list[int]]]] = {}
+        self.transfers_not_processed: set[TransferId] = set()
+
+    def add_new_req(
+        self,
+        request_id: ReqId,
+        local_block_ids: list[list[int]],
+        kv_transfer_params: dict[str, Any],
+        load_remote_cache: bool = True,
+    ):
+        transfer_id = kv_transfer_params["transfer_id"]
+        if load_remote_cache:
+            remote_engine_id = kv_transfer_params["remote_engine_id"]
+            self.reqs_to_recv[remote_engine_id][request_id] = PullReqMeta(
+                d_req_id=request_id,
+                local_block_ids=local_block_ids,
+                remote_engine_id=remote_engine_id,
+                remote_bootstrap_addr=kv_transfer_params["remote_bootstrap_addr"],
+                transfer_id=transfer_id,
+            )
+        else:
+            self.reqs_to_send[request_id] = (transfer_id, local_block_ids)

-            metadata.reqs_to_send or metadata.reqs_not_processed

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from enum import IntEnum
+
+import msgspec
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake.metadata import (
+    ReqId,
+    TransferId,
+)
+
+
+class MooncakeXferMetadata(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    omit_defaults=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    remote_hostname: str
+    remote_port: int
+    remote_tp_size: int
+    remote_tp_rank: int
+    req_blocks: dict[ReqId, tuple[TransferId, list[list[int]]]]
+    kv_caches_base_addr: list[int]
+    block_lens: list[int]
+    kv_block_lens: list[int]
+    registered_layer_names: list[str] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    registered_layer_indices: list[int] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    registered_group_indices: list[int] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    # Parallel to registered regions. Each entry is the groups that share
+    # that region. Empty means the peer did not send the field.
+    registered_shared_group_ids: list[list[int]] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    # Byte offset of each registered view from its block row. -1 means the
+    # peer did not send the field, so the run must not be promoted.
+    registered_row_offsets: list[int] = msgspec.field(default_factory=list)
+    remote_pp_size: int = 1
+    # Random per register_kv_caches, so ids never repeat across restarts.
+    # 0 means the peer sends the layout on every pull.
+    layout_id: int = 0
+
+
+class MooncakeXferResponseStatus(IntEnum):
+    # Transfer finished
+    FINISH = 0
+    # Continue to receive
+    CONTINUE = 1
+    # Something wrong, see err_msg
+    ERROR = 2
+    # P does not hold the layout for this layout_id; resend it.
+    # Only sent for pulls with a nonzero layout_id and no layout.
+    LAYOUT_MISS = 3
+
+
+class MooncakeXferResponse(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    omit_defaults=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    status: MooncakeXferResponseStatus
+    ok_reqs: list[ReqId] | None = None
+    err_reqs: list[ReqId] | None = None
+    err_msg: str | None = None
+    # The pull's layout_id once P holds that layout. D omits the layout only
+    # after seeing it, so a P that predates this field always gets it.
+    layout_id: int = 0
